headline: Council considers Hoʻonani Village land bills, accessory dwelling units and noise fines

meeting.summary: Bills for the Hoʻonani Village project would change 163.443 acres in Kahului from agriculture to business and multi-family; Bill 163 needs a Maui public hearing before final reading. An amendment raising noise fines in Bill 119 passed seven ayes, two noes.
meeting.recap: A testifier asked the council to wait for a final environmental impact statement before acting on Bills 163 and 164.[[0:26:32]] The council approved that recommendation with six ayes, one no and two members excused.[[0:51:59]] Bill 78 would allow two accessory dwelling units, or extra small homes, on residential lots.[[0:52:28]] Bill 84 would cap bed and breakfast homes on Molokaʻi at five.[[0:57:29]] Resolution 26-84 would send land use bills for the EC Pāʻia Town project to the Maui Planning Commission.[[0:59:38]] A committee change requires the project's workforce rental units to stay affordable forever.[[1:00:16]] The council voted eight ayes, zero noes to discharge, or release, Bill 119 from committee.[[1:10:02]] The chair moved to replace Bill 119 with a version that raises fines for noise violations.[[1:11:35]] The amendment passed with seven ayes and two noes.[[1:19:00]]
decided: The vote on this motion was not captured in the recording.
meeting.next: A public hearing on Bill 163 is to be held on Maui before second and final reading.

issues.why: A council member said housing is needed more now than ever, with families living in cars and at the beach.

deadlines.t: Counties must enact an ordinance allowing at least two accessory dwelling units.

issues.brief: The bills would change the land's community plan designation from agriculture to business and multi-family.[[#1]] A council member said the action would not create housing right away but would continue the conversation.[[#2]]
